page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-24-lssd is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 24 vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 186.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.75 GB per core. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, consisting of 1343 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across four local drives. The x86_64 architecture includes advanced CPU instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated tile and integer operations, alongside hardware-assisted cryptography via AES and SHA extensions.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with the single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates placing in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core testing also registers in the top 10% tier, while multi-core performance and image processing capabilities fall within the top 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is robust, reaching 2024.01 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, though it drops to 153.52 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Standard database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput align with average mid-tier benchmarks, indicating stable execution under typical transactional loads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-24-lssd offers a high-density resource profile by combining substantial memory capacity with fast local NVMe storage on a dedicated compute tier. This configuration avoids the latency overhead of network-attached storage, making it highly suitable for memory-intensive and I/O-sensitive workloads. Recommended applications include high-performance database hosting, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data processing pipelines, and software compilation tasks that benefit from both high-speed local storage and advanced vector instruction sets.
